claims.text: The proposed baseline is an as-deposited, continuous nanoscale thin film of non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy alloy.
The controlled intervention is lithographic patterning into nanoribbons with widths at or below approximately 200 nm while preserving thickness and composition.
Reducing the lateral dimensions increases the edge-to-volume ratio.
The increased edge-to-volume ratio promotes magnetic domain-wall pinning in FeMnNiGeSi nanoribbons.
Nanoribbon edges induce local stress variations.
Lateral confinement alters the magnetic domain structure.
Edge effects increase local magnetic anisotropy.
Increased local anisotropy contributes to broader magnetic hysteresis.
Increased domain-wall pinning contributes to broader magnetic hysteresis.
Lateral confinement restricts thermal transport and slows heat dissipation during cycling.
Slower heat dissipation reduces the ability of the nanoribbons to undergo rapid magnetocaloric switching.
Relative to continuous films, sub-200 nm nanoribbons will exhibit wider magnetic hysteresis under otherwise identical low-field cycles.
Relative to continuous films, sub-200 nm nanoribbons will exhibit a lower peak magnetic entropy change under low-field cycles.
Heat-transfer limitations inherently constrain cycling frequency in nanoscale films.
Using identical thermal cycling rates and applied-field amplitudes permits comparison between continuous and patterned samples.
The proposed confinement effect applies under low applied fields, heat-transfer-limited cycling frequencies, and substantially reduced lateral dimensions.
Intrinsic defects or compositional inhomogeneities may compete with the proposed edge-confinement effects.
Magnetization-versus-field measurements can characterize hysteresis loops in high-entropy-alloy thin films.
